question: Where should the latency for the scoring report actually be measured?
setup: same 100 cases of frozen/d2_v1_1_val, same weights (A3 candidate v1), same B3 code; only the environment differs

io_probe.method: read + PIL decode/thumbnail of the same 20 JPEGs from the Windows-drive mount vs a copy inside the container
io_probe.note: raw read is about 200x slower and decode+resize about 14x slower through the mount

conclusion: The first in-container run looked 6x slower end to end (89.2 ms vs 14.6 ms) purely because the dataset was read through a Windows-drive bind mount. With the same data inside the container the official image is the fastest of the three (E2E P50 12.9 ms, P95 15.2 ms). Two consequences: (1) the scoring material can quote an official-image measurement now, and it sits comfortably inside the 150 ms end-to-end threshold; (2) anyone measuring inside Docker on Windows must copy the dataset into the container first, otherwise the latency is inflated by roughly 6x.

claim_scope.note: X86 workstation measurement inside the official OpenExplorer image; not a board number.
